about:
Commercial Plastics Corp. operates from Arlington, Washington. The company has over 30 years of experience in the plastic fabrication industry, though a specific founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm specializes in custom plastic fabrication and manufacturing, producing items such as cutting boards, award cases, model boxes, signs, displays, and polycarbonate floor mats. It maintains a wide inventory of sheet plastics—including acrylic, polycarbonate, ABS, and polyethylene—and offers precision cutting to customer specifications. Its skilled technicians handle projects ranging from single prototypes to large-scale assemblies, supported by a state-of-the-art facility equipped with current technology, a large sheeting inventory, and integrated storage and distribution capabilities.

Commercial Plastics serves marine, retail, commercial, and industrial sectors, providing custom solutions for each. The company emphasizes close collaboration with clients to meet specific application requirements across these markets.

The company positions itself as an all-in-one resource, combining skilled professionals, modern technology, extensive material inventory, manufacturing, storage, and distribution under one roof. It cites a commitment to exceptional customer service and high-quality products as core differentiators.

name: Commercial Radio Company
old_description: Mica capacitors hold an important place in RF engineering due to their stable performance and long-term reliability. These components use natural mica as the dielectric, which supports accurate capacitance values with minimal drift. In high-frequency designs, small variations can change circuit behavior, so engineers look for parts that protect performance.
about:
Commercial Radio Company, Inc. is based in Cavendish, Vermont. Founded in 1970 by Dan Churchill, an engineer with a background in radio transmission, the company began as a supplier of mica capacitors for broadcast and transmitter applications. Today it operates as a second-generation business.

The company acts as the world's largest stocking distributor for Cornell-Dubilier (CDM) mica capacitors. It maintains a comprehensive inventory covering types 271, 272, 273, 291, 292, 293, 294, as well as HT, HK, AT, and AK series. The capacitors use natural mica dielectric, offering stable capacitance with minimal drift, resistance to moisture, heat, and voltage drift. The firm ships from its Vermont facility and serves customers globally.

Customers span aerospace and defense, medical equipment, counter-drone technology, electronic warfare, wind and solar energy, electric-vehicle charging stations, military applications, and broadcast radio stations. The company cites these sectors as typical applications for its mica capacitor lines.

Commercial Radio Company emphasizes its Made-in-USA supply chain, competitive pricing, and large on-hand inventory as differentiators. It was started to provide reliable capacitor solutions for broadcast engineers and has expanded to meet next-generation semiconductor needs.

name: Complete Cable Company LLC
old_description: Complete Cable Company LLC manufactures custom wire harnesses and cable assemblies for OEM applications across a wide range of industries. We support customers from prototype development through repeat production with a focus on quality, responsiveness, and dependable lead times.
about:
Complete Cable Company LLC operates from St. Joseph, Michigan, as a family-owned manufacturer of custom wire harnesses and cable assemblies. The business is led by co-owners Rob Kasun and Jon Kasun, who manage operations, quoting, production, and quality oversight.

The company specializes in build-to-print manufacturing for OEM applications, handling prototype, low-volume, and repeat production runs. Its capabilities include wire cutting, stripping, crimping, and harness assembly across 14–22 AWG gauges with PVC and SRPVC insulation, as well as cable routing, bundling, labeling, and kitting. Every assembly undergoes 100% continuity and hi-pot testing on a Cirris 4250 tester, with results traceable to each production run.

Complete Cable serves the automotive, appliance manufacturing, industrial equipment, and electromechanical sectors, supplying OEMs with power distribution cables, custom test harnesses, and patch cords engineered to exact specifications.

The firm emphasizes direct access to ownership for fast decisions, quoting typically within 48 business hours, and expedited prototype builds. A small, agile team focuses on hands-on oversight, process-controlled assembly, and dependable lead times tied to material availability.

name: Complexus Medical
old_description: Complexus Medical is a full-service contract manufacturer of medical devices and healthcare products.
about:
Complexus Medical traces its roots to 1968 when F&F Machine Specialties opened as a small tool-and-die shop in a Mishawaka, Indiana basement. The company rebranded as Complexus Medical and, under the leadership of Michael Behrens, has grown into a full-service contract manufacturer with two modern facilities in Mishawaka and Plymouth, Indiana. A 2013 expansion doubled the Mishawaka headquarters, and a second site was added in 2021 to support increasing demand.

The company provides end-to-end contract manufacturing for medical devices and healthcare products. Its service portfolio covers clean-room assembly, sub-assembly and final assembly, custom kitting and sterile barrier packaging, sterilization coordination (EtO, gamma, and e-beam), supply chain management, regulatory support, and rapid prototyping with tooling development. Complexus handles all welding, finishing, and assembly in-house, enabling control over quality and lead times. The firm reports more than 500 products manufactured and emphasizes FDA-compliant documentation throughout.

Complexus serves medical device OEMs, with a historic focus on the orthopedic device and implant industry. Customers rely on the company for complex instruments that involve multiple components, tight tolerances, and intricate geometry. Typical projects include surgical instrument assemblies, procedure packs, tray configurations, and sterile barrier systems that require validated sterilization processes.

The company positions itself on three differentiators: decades of experience with difficult orthopedic instruments, full in-house control of welding, finishing, and assembly, and a "right-sized" structure that is small enough to manage every project detail yet large enough to deliver at scale. These factors, combined with full-service sterilization coordination and two Indiana locations, form the basis of its value proposition.

about:
Component Dynamics operates from Portsmouth, New Hampshire, as an independent supplier of electronic components. The company focuses on obsolete, last-time-buy, and hard-to-find parts, serving customers through a global network of partners and three accredited hubs in North America, Europe, and Asia.

The firm provides component sourcing, excess inventory solutions, obsolescence management, cost savings programs, and warehousing and fulfillment services. Its multi-stage inspection process and vendor rating program aim to eliminate counterfeit risk, while an integrated management system governs quality, environmental, and safety standards. The company reports 96 percent customer satisfaction, 95 percent on-time delivery, and a less than 1 percent RMA rate.

Component Dynamics serves aerospace, defense, government, and electronics manufacturers, evidenced by AS9120B and AS6081 certifications and participation in the Government Industry Data Exchange Program. Customers include high-profile manufacturers seeking allocated or obsolete semiconductors and other electronic components.

The company emphasizes its independence, flexibility, and round-the-clock global team as differentiators, with a stated commitment to continuous improvement, counterfeit mitigation, and environmental protection through its certifications.

name: Compulink Cable Assemblies Inc.
old_description: COMPULINK SPECIALIZES IN WIRE HARNESS ASSEMBLY AND CUSTOM MOLDED CABLE ASSEMBLIES
about:
Compulink Cable Assemblies Inc. was founded in 1984 in St. Petersburg, Florida. The company specializes in wire harness assembly and custom molded cable assemblies for a range of high-reliability markets.

Compulink manufactures cable and wire harness assemblies that incorporate printed circuit boards, fans, switches, power supplies, and panel assemblies. Its capabilities span wire harness assembly, custom overmolding, coaxial and RF cable assembly, electromechanical box builds, control panel fabrication, and low-pressure molding. The company operates a crimp quality assurance lab equipped with a Schleuniger MicroGraph System for cross-sectional analysis, and offers engineering support, rapid prototyping, quick-turn production, and first-article inspection. Production runs from prototype through low-rate initial to full volume.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers and military contractors across defense, medical, industrial, commercial, transportation, and renewable energy sectors. Its ITAR-registered, AS9100D- and ISO 9001:2015-certified facility produces military harnesses and molded assemblies deployed in defense equipment worldwide, as well as RF and coaxial cables for commercial and industrial applications.

Compulink emphasizes a performance-based culture built on lean manufacturing, automation, and continuous improvement. Every team member is trained to IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship standards, with in-house Level A instructors. The company welcomes customer audits of its quality system and facilities, and maintains documented procedures for traceability, corrective action, and crimp monitoring.

old_description: As a command center solution provider, we focus exclusively on mission-critical projects, with an unrivaled depth of knowledge that enables us to consistently deliver high-performing command centers. We work to earn your trust by making every experience with Constant exceptional.
about:
Constant Technologies is headquartered in North Kingstown, Rhode Island. The company has over 40 years of experience in mission-critical command center solutions, though a specific founding year is not disclosed. President Brad Righi leads the organization, which operates as a global provider of integrated operations centers.

The firm designs, manufactures, and installs complete command and control environments, including video wall systems, specialized console workstations, and audiovisual integration. Its in-house capabilities span architecture, systems engineering, product engineering, and manufacturing, with a certified design team comprising AIA-certified architects and CTS-D-accredited A/V engineers. Constant manages projects from discovery through commissioning and provides 24/7 global support. The company reports more than 5,000 installations across 20-plus countries, with a multinational network of offices and partner locations.

Constant serves technology, finance, public safety, utility, government, healthcare, fleet operations, brand protection, and retail sectors. Named clients include Meta, CVS Health, Boeing, and the U.S. Department of Defense, along with numerous police departments and public safety agencies such as the Albany Police Department and Aurora Police Department.

The company emphasizes its unwavering dedication to quality as a differentiator, citing a robust quality management system and a culture that prioritizes workmanship. Its proven process — discovery, design, execution, commissioning, and ongoing support — is intended to deliver reliable, high-performing centers that operate continuously under mission-critical demands.
